Entries.Original: Good, you're all here.
To begin, allow me to brief you on everything that we currently know about what you will be up against.
Listen to the briefing?
Extra carefully!|Request a summary
Summary, please!
Why?
Because, I'm gonna freaking wet myself!
Why didn't you go before...?
Very well. Then I'll give you the abridged version.
You actually took her request?!
The Cancers possess extraordinary regenerative abilities. The most popular theory is that they procure their energy from a higher dimension—one we are not yet capable of perceiving.
Their intelligence is comparable to animals on Earth: they act on instinct, but they prey on intelligent beings.
Regarding their attacks, we believe they are possible due to the aforementioned energy source.
To counter this, we've developed the Seraph Defense Function, otherwise referred to as "deflectors."
Deflectors redirect the vectors of the Cancers' attacks, significantly decreasing, if not nullifying, the damage.
However, they can only withstand so much damage. After that point, there is nothing standing between you and certain doom.
No way...
When that happens...
As such, once your deflectors expire, retreat immediately. No exceptions.
Summoning a Seraph weapon also increases one's physical capabilities exponentially. This is what allowed you to fight on the battlefield yesterday without proper training.
However, there are downsides as well. Continued use of one's Seraph will trigger a nosebleed.
Further use will result in certain death. A single night's rest is all that's required to recover, so should your nose bleed, retreat to a safe zone immediately.
Now, regarding humanity, which you are tasked with protecting...
The majority of mankind is currently in hiding from the Cancers, eking out a living in bases called "domes."
The Cancers appear to differentiate friend from foe via wavelengths they emit from their exoskeletons.
With this in mind, humanity has utilized the nature of said exoskeletons to build defensive perimeters and avoid detection.
That being said, the domes are not a fail-safe solution.
Therefore, one of the Seraph Squadron's duties is to protect these domes.
However, dome inhabitants and squadron members are not allowed to interact. Any violations will result in strict punishment in accordance with martial law.
Why can't we interact with them?
You must understand that Seraphim are dangerous weapons. A single mistake could result in civilian casualties.
That's all for now. Is everything absolutely clear?
Not one bit.
I figured as much. You can learn more by browsing the reference materials in the archives during free time.
I explained this earlier, but it is important and bears repeating. Understood?
Your enemy is the Cancer—organisms that infect the "body" of space.
Until recently, the Cancers were completely immune to every weapon humanity threw at them.
Mankind suffered one loss after the next, until we lost half the Earth's land mass to the Cancer.
And Japan was no exception. Kyushu and Hokkaido were obliterated, and the remaining islands were one step away from the same fate. But, on the brink of ruin, a new weapon was born: the Seraph.
Right?
All you did was repeat her speech verbatim. Not a single new piece of information has left your lips.
Precisely. Samples were taken, but no laser or bomb could scratch its impenetrable surface. Or rather, any scratch that appeared was quickly repaired.
The most popular theory is that Cancers procure their energy from a higher dimension—one we are not yet capable of perceiving.
Oh.
Not even a little shook? That's what we're up against.
Only Seraphim are capable of reaching that dimension and cutting off their energy at the source.
How did we discover that?
Thanks to the research of our scientists.
If humans can't detect that dimension, how could they verify Seraphim could reach it to begin with?
Our scientists are more capable than you realize.
Oh.
Even supposing they receive their energy from a higher dimension, their intelligence is comparable to animals on Earth.
They act on instinct, but they prey on intelligent beings.
Regarding their attacks, we believe they are possible due to the aforementioned energy source.
To counter this, we've developed the Seraph Defense Function, otherwise referred to as "deflectors."
Deflectors redirect the vectors of the Cancers' attacks, significantly decreasing, if not nullifying, the damage.
Huh? If we've got something like that, why not just charge at 'em till they drop?
It's not that simple.
Deflectors can only withstand so much damage. After that point, there is nothing standing between you and certain doom.
No way...
When that happens...
As such, once your deflectors expire, retreat immediately. No exceptions.
What? Wouldn't you wanna help your friends when they're in danger?
Out of the question.
Cold, much?
You all are too valuable to throw away your lives like that.
Summoning a Seraph weapon increases one's physical capabilities exponentially. That is what allowed you to fight on the battlefield yesterday without proper training.
The future of humanity rests with you, the Seraph Squadron. Never forget that.
'Course not, how could I? As humanity's savior, I'll take down more Cancers than anyone!
However, it's not all sunshine and rainbows. There is one other scenario in which you could die.
Continued use of one's Seraph without rest will trigger a nosebleed. This signals that the user is in an incredibly dangerous state.
Should you trigger a nosebleed, retreat to a safe zone immediately. A single night's rest is all that's required.
Retreat from a wimpy nosebleed?
Seraphim are extraordinarily powerful. Wielding them comes with great risk.
As such, be on alert for any nosebleeds amongst your squad.
"Teacher! So-and-so has a nosebleed!" ...Like that?
Yes.
What is this, elementary?
Now, regarding humanity, which you are tasked with protecting...
While you were undergoing assessment after being scouted, the situation has changed quite dramatically.
The majority of mankind is currently in hiding from the Cancers, eking out a living in bases called "domes."
Huh? THAT many people? Seriously?
You saw the Population Tracker, yes?\nFewer than 10 million people survive.
Yeah, I still can't really picture it.
You said "in hiding." How do they hide from the Cancers?
The Cancers appear to differentiate friend from foe via wavelengths they emit from their exoskeletons.
With this in mind, humanity has utilized the nature of said exoskeletons to build defensive perimeters and avoid detection.
Couldn't we just wear their eggs-o-skeletons as armor and charge at them full speed ahead?
Unfortunately for us, the Cancers are not that stupid.
They might initially prove useful in a surprise maneuver, but we would quickly be labeled as enemy combatants.
And then we would be forced to fight while wearing heavy exoskeletons.
So much for my eureka moment.
Did you really think they hadn't tried that already?
That being said, the domes are not a fail-safe solution.
The domes have occasionally been spotted by Cancer scouts or found themselves in the paths of large-scale Cancers.
Under such conditions, it is the Seraph Squadron's duty to protect the domes.
However, dome inhabitants and squadron members are not allowed to interact. Any violations will result in strict punishment in accordance with martial law.
Why can't we interact with them?
You must understand that Seraphim are dangerous weapons. A single mistake could result in civilian casualties.
That's true. These Seraph thingies kinda are no joke...
Moreover, with your ability to wield Seraphim, you are the hope of all mankind. What do you think would happen if you visited the domes?
I'm used to signing autographs.
That is not the issue at hand. It would cause a commotion.
Us? Really?
Yes. At present, disrupting the order in the domes is too risky. Heed that well.
Okaaay!
What is this, elementary?
